title: SUM evaluates all direct-argument errors before held reference/array errors, and overflow does not mask later errors
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, SUM checks direct scalar arguments (including text-to-number coercion #VALUE!) in argument order before reporting any error held inside a reference or array argument, so =SUM(A1:B2,"a") and =SUM({1,#REF!},"a") both return #VALUE! even when B1 holds #N/A. Among held errors, SUM follows argument order, and a numeric overflow to #NUM! does not stop reading later arguments, so =SUM(9.99999999999999E+307,9.99999999999999E+307,B1) returns #N/A.
basis: Recorded in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in cfunc_m1_2 (sheet error_order rows 69-87, with #N/A in B1 and #DIV/0! in A2) and matched across 1,211 of 1,211 full-bank SUM witness rows.
